questions.question: What is Splunk and what problem does it solve?
options: A platform for searching, monitoring, and analyzing machine-generated data (logs, metrics, events) — indexes any data from any source, makes it searchable in real-time. Use cases: security monitoring (SIEM), operational intelligence, IT troubleshooting, business analytics
questions.explanation: Splunk: collect logs/metrics from servers, apps, network devices, cloud services. Index and make searchable. Create dashboards, alerts, reports. Core value: machine data analytics without predefined schema — search any field. Deployment: Splunk Enterprise (on-prem), Splunk Cloud, Splunk Free (limited).

questions.question: What is the Splunk SPL (Search Processing Language) basic structure?
options: search terms | command1 args | command2 args — starts with search (implicit), pipe (|) chains commands, each command transforms previous results. Example: index=web status=404 | stats count by host | sort -count | head 10
questions.explanation: SPL pipeline: (1) search: find events (index, keywords, field=value). (2) Pipe commands: transform results. Key commands: stats (aggregate), eval (calculate), where (filter), timechart (time-based chart), dedup (remove duplicates), table (select fields), rename (rename field), rex (regex extraction).

questions.question: What is a Splunk index and why is data organization important?
options: A repository of Splunk data — separate indexes for different data types (web, security, network) allow: access controls (role can only access certain indexes), better search performance, separate retention policies. Default index: main
questions.explanation: Index: data bucket. Common indexes: main (default), security, web, windows, linux. Specify in search: index=security. Multiple: index=web OR index=apache. Wildcard: index=web*. Retention: different per index (security: 1 year, debug: 7 days). Role-based access: restrict index access per role.

questions.question: What is the Splunk stats command and what are common aggregation functions?
options: Aggregate search results — stats count, sum(field), avg(field), max(field), min(field), dc(field) (distinct count), values(field) (list unique values) BY field1, field2. Example: stats count by status, host
questions.explanation: stats: aggregate events into statistical results. count: number of events. sum(bytes): total bytes. avg(response_time): average. dc(user): distinct user count. values(error): all unique error messages. by clause: group by fields. Multiple stats in one command: stats count, avg(duration), max(size) by host.

questions.question: What is the Splunk timechart command?
options: Creates a time-series chart — similar to stats but X-axis is always time. timechart span=1h count by status: count events per hour broken down by status field. Useful for: trends over time, comparing metrics across time, dashboards
questions.explanation: timechart: X-axis = time buckets. span: bucket size (1m, 1h, 1d, 1w). timechart count: events per time bucket. timechart avg(cpu) by host: average CPU per host per time bucket. limit=5: top 5 values (rest grouped as OTHER). Always generates chart visualization in Splunk UI.

questions.question: What is the Splunk eval command?
options: Creates or modifies field values using expressions — eval new_field=expression. Math: eval total=quantity*price. String: eval full_name=first_name.' '.last_name. Conditionals: eval status_text=if(status==200,'OK','Error'). case(): multiple conditions
questions.explanation: eval: calculate new fields. Functions: if(condition, true_val, false_val), case(cond1, val1, cond2, val2,...), len(string), lower()/upper(), substr(), round(num, places), now() (current time), strftime(time, format). eval: adds to results without consuming events (unlike stats which collapses to one row per group).

questions.question: What is the Splunk rex command?
options: Extracts fields from events using named regex groups — rex field=_raw '(?<username>\w+) logged in'. Extracts 'username' field from raw event. Also: rex mode=sed to perform search/replace on field values
questions.explanation: rex: regex field extraction. Named groups: (?<field_name>pattern). Example: rex field=_raw 'user=(?<user>\S+) src=(?<src_ip>\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)'. Applies to every event in pipeline. Alternative: Field Extractions (props.conf EXTRACT-) for persistent extractions at index time. rex at search time: flexible, no config needed.

questions.question: What is a Splunk Lookup and how does it enrich data?
options: A reference table (CSV or KV Store) that enriches events with additional context — lookup user_info.csv username OUTPUT department, manager_name. Adds fields from external table based on matching field value
questions.explanation: Lookups: | lookup filename.csv match_field OUTPUT enrichment_fields. Example: | lookup asset_inventory.csv ip_address OUTPUT hostname, owner, criticality. KV Store: dynamic lookups (can be updated via API/SPL). Automatic lookups: configured in transforms.conf, apply automatically at search time. Enrich: add hostname to IP, add user info, add asset classification.

questions.question: What is the Splunk where command vs search command?
options: search: filters events matching keywords/field=value (boolean, wildcards) — runs at the beginning of pipeline. where: filters results using eval expressions — runs anywhere in pipeline (post-transformation). where supports: functions, comparisons, math. search: simpler, faster for index filtering
questions.explanation: search keyword (or implicit start): leverages index for performance. where (after pipe): evaluate field expressions. Examples: | where status>=400 AND status<500. | where len(error_msg)>100. | where isnull(username). Cannot use where at start (before any events returned). Use where after stats/eval when filtering transformed results.

questions.question: What is a Splunk Saved Search vs a Dashboard?
options: Saved Search: stores a SPL query with schedule, alert action, and permissions. Runs on schedule or on-demand. Can trigger: email alert, webhook, create notable event. Dashboard: visual display of multiple panels (charts, tables, single values) — can include saved searches or inline searches
questions.explanation: Saved searches: run on schedule (every 5 min, daily). Alert actions: email, webhook, create ITSI episode, trigger script. Accelerated: results cached for dashboards. Dashboards: XML or Simple XML + CSS/JS. Panels: each panel has own search. Dashboard inputs: time range, dropdown, text box. Share: per app or globally.

questions.question: What is Splunk's sourcetype and how does it affect parsing?
options: Identifies the format/type of data — tells Splunk how to parse and break events (line breaking, timestamp recognition, field extractions). Examples: access_combined (Apache logs), syslog, WinEventLog:Security, cisco:asa. Defined automatically or manually
questions.explanation: Sourcetype: key metadata. Determines: event breaking (multiline), timestamp parsing, field extractions (from props.conf), REPORT/EXTRACT patterns. Always filter with sourcetype for accuracy: index=web sourcetype=access_combined. Common: access_combined, syslog, WinEventLog:Security, linux_secure, cisco:asa, aws:cloudtrail.

questions.question: What are Splunk's main metadata fields?
options: _time (timestamp of event), _raw (original unparsed event text), host (where event originated), source (file or input path), sourcetype (data format/type), index (which index stored). These exist on every event, cannot be removed
questions.explanation: Default fields on every event: _time (epoch), _raw (full event text), host (server name/IP), source (file path, port, etc.), sourcetype (log format). index (which index). These are always available without configuration. Other fields: extracted at index time (props/transforms) or search time.

questions.question: What is Splunk Alert and what types are available?
options: Triggered when a saved search result meets a condition — types: Scheduled (run on schedule, alert if result count > threshold), Real-time (continuous monitoring, alert immediately). Alert actions: email, webhook, script, PagerDuty, Jira, ServiceNow, ITSI notable event
questions.explanation: Alerts: Settings > Searches, Reports, and Alerts. Per-result alert: fires for each result row. Number of results alert: fires when count exceeds threshold. Field value alert: fires on specific field value. Throttling: prevent alert spam. Alert actions: email notification, Slack webhook, ServiceNow incident creation, custom scripts.

questions.question: What is Splunk's index-time vs search-time processing?
options: Index-time: processing when data is ingested (line breaking, timestamp parsing, field extraction via INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS). Search-time: field extractions happen when you search (EXTRACT-/REPORT- in props.conf, rex command). Index-time: faster search, larger index. Search-time: flexible, doesn't bloat index
questions.explanation: Index-time extractions: field values stored in index → fast search. But: increases index size, changes require re-indexing. Search-time extractions: performed at query time → slower but flexible. Best practice: use search-time for most extractions (flexibility). Index-time: high-cardinality fields you filter on frequently. Automatic kv_mode: common key=value auto-extracted at search time.

questions.question: What is the Splunk dedup command?
options: Removes duplicate events based on one or more field values — dedup username: keeps first event per username. dedup username, status: keep first event per username+status combination. Options: sortby (-_time), consecutive (only remove adjacent duplicates)
questions.explanation: dedup: remove duplicate results. By default: keeps first occurrence (by _time, oldest first). dedup username keepempty=true: keep nulls. dedup 5 url: keep top 5 results per url. Useful for: find unique users, latest status per host, one sample event per error type. More efficient alternative: stats first(field) by key.

questions.question: What is a Splunk Data Model and why is it used?
options: A hierarchical structure that organizes data into datasets (searches) used by Pivot and ITSM-style reporting — models speed up searches via Data Model Acceleration (pre-computed summaries). Enterprise Security: all detections built on data models
questions.explanation: Data Models: define event/transaction/search datasets hierarchically. Pivot: drag-and-drop report builder using data models (no SPL needed). Acceleration: summarize index data into data model acceleration — makes time-series searches very fast. Splunk ES: Authentication, Network Traffic, Malware data models are foundation.

questions.question: What is the Splunk transaction command?
options: Groups related events into transactions based on field values and time constraints — transaction session_id maxspan=30m maxpause=5m. Calculates: duration, eventcount per transaction. Example: group all web events for same session_id within 30 minutes
questions.explanation: transaction: group events by field + time. Fields: session_id, transaction_id, username. maxspan: max total transaction duration. maxpause: max gap between events in transaction. Returns: one result per transaction with duration and eventcount. Slower than stats — use stats when possible. Good for: user sessions, workflow tracking.

questions.question: What is Splunk's Search Head Clustering (SHC)?
options: A group of Splunk search heads that work together — all have same configuration, share knowledge objects (saved searches, dashboards), and load-balance user searches. Deployer: pushes configuration to all cluster members. Captain: coordinates cluster
questions.explanation: SHC: 3+ search heads + deployer. Deployer: pushes apps/config to cluster members (not direct config). Captain: elected leader, coordinates replication. Knowledge objects: replicated across all members. Users: connect through load balancer, any member can handle search. High availability: member fails, others continue.

questions.question: What is Splunk's Indexer Clustering (SmartStore)?
options: A group of indexers that replicate data for high availability — replication factor (how many copies), search factor (searchable copies). Cluster Master/Manager: coordinates. Each bucket replicated N times. Peer failure: automatic search continues on other peers
questions.explanation: Indexer cluster: manager node + peer nodes. Replication factor (RF): how many copies of each bucket (RF=3 means 3 copies). Search factor (SF): how many searchable copies. Peer failure: automatic failover. Site-aware: multi-site clustering for DR. SmartStore: tiered storage (warm data on S3, hot on local SSD).

questions.question: What is the Splunk tstats command and when is it used?
options: Fast search command that queries index-level metadata and Data Model Accelerations — much faster than regular searches for large data volumes. Works on: tsidx files, data model accelerations. Limited: only pre-extracted fields at index time
questions.explanation: tstats: fastest search for large datasets. | tstats count WHERE index=web by host, status: counts from tsidx metadata without reading event _raw. Requires: index-time field extraction or data model acceleration. Splunk ES: tstats on accelerated data models for fast correlation searches. Limitation: can't use eval or rex.

questions.question: What is the Splunk top and rare commands?
options: top: returns most common values of a field with count and percentage — top limit=10 field1, field2. rare: opposite — returns least common values. Both show: value, count, percent. Quick for initial data exploration without full stats
questions.explanation: top: top N most frequent field values. top url: top 10 URLs by count. top limit=20 status by host: top 20 statuses per host. rare: least frequent (anomaly detection). Both show count and percentage. Default limit: 10. Equivalent stats: stats count by field | sort -count.

questions.question: What is Splunk Field Extraction (regex vs delimiter)?
options: Automatic or manual extraction of fields from _raw event text — Regex: extract using patterns (free-form log formats). Delimiter: split on character (CSV-style). Configured in: UI via Field Extractor, or props.conf/transforms.conf for persistent config
questions.explanation: Field Extractor: Settings > Fields > Field Extractions. Interactive: highlight field in event → auto-generate regex. Regex extraction: EXTRACT-fieldname in props.conf. Delimiter: FIELDALIAS or CSV parsing. KV auto-extract: key=value pairs auto-extracted. IFX (Interactive Field Extractor): click-based regex builder in UI.

questions.question: What is the Splunk inputlookup and outputlookup commands?
options: inputlookup: reads lookup table as search results (instead of from events). | inputlookup asset_inventory.csv. outputlookup: writes search results to a lookup file. | outputlookup blocked_ips.csv. Use for: read/write lookup files, populate lookups from Splunk data
questions.explanation: inputlookup: treats lookup as data source. | inputlookup users.csv WHERE department='IT': filter lookup. Useful for: analyzing lookup data itself, cross-referencing. outputlookup: save search results back to lookup. | top 100 src_ip | outputlookup top_ips.csv. Creates/overwrites lookup file. Use for: build dynamic threat lists from searches.

questions.question: What is Splunk's Common Information Model (CIM)?
options: A standardized field-naming convention that normalizes data from different sources into consistent field names — email_from, src_ip, dest_port, user. Enables: correlation across different sourcetypes. CIM Add-on: includes data models built on these field names
questions.explanation: CIM: normalized field names. Instead of: source_address (Cisco) and SrcIP (Windows) and src (Fortigate) — CIM uses src for all. CIM Add-on: maps vendor fields to CIM fields (field aliases). Data models use CIM fields. Splunk ES: all detections use CIM — if your data isn't CIM-mapped, ES misses it. Key: map data to CIM at ingestion.

questions.question: What is Splunk Enterprise Security (ES)?
options: Splunk's SIEM app — built on Splunk platform, adds: threat detection (correlation searches = notable events), investigations (incident review workflow), risk-based alerting, threat intelligence framework, asset and identity management, user behavior analytics
questions.explanation: Splunk ES: security operations platform. Correlation searches: SPL searches running every few minutes generating notable events (alerts). Incident Review: triage, investigate, assign, resolve notable events. Risk Framework: assign risk scores to users/assets, alert on risk threshold breach. Requires: CIM-normalized data for out-of-box detections.

questions.question: What is the Splunk join command and its limitations?
options: Combines results from two searches based on matching field — similar to SQL JOIN. Limitations: performance-intensive (should use lookup instead when possible), limits: 50,000 results by default, only one join sub-search
questions.explanation: join: | join type=inner/outer/left username [search index=hr earliest=-1d latest=now | table username, department]. Slow: don't use for large datasets. Better alternatives: lookup (for static data), append+stats, subsearch. join type=outer: keep non-matching rows from left side. type=inner: only matching rows.

questions.question: What is Splunk's summary indexing?
options: Stores pre-aggregated search results in a summary index — scheduled search runs, saves results to summary index. Dashboard queries summary index instead of raw data: much faster. Use for: long-term trend data, executive dashboards, accelerating slow searches
questions.explanation: Summary indexing: scheduled search → | collect index=summary. Subsequent searches: index=summary. Advantages: lightning-fast dashboard performance, retain aggregated data beyond raw data retention. Downside: management overhead, data drift if source data changes. Data Model Acceleration: more automated alternative.

questions.question: What are Splunk Macro searches?
options: Reusable SPL query fragments defined with a name — reference in searches with backticks: `my_macro`. Can accept arguments: `my_macro(value1,value2)`. Use for: standardize complex filters, promote consistency across searches
questions.explanation: Search macros: Settings > Advanced Search > Search Macros. Name: my_filter_macro. Definition: index=web status>=400. Usage: `my_filter_macro` | stats count by host. Arguments: `calculate_rate(field)` → definition: eval rate=field/60. Backtick expansion: inline replacement. Use for: company-wide standard searches, complex filters used repeatedly.

questions.question: What is the Splunk chart command vs timechart?
options: chart: creates a chart with specified X and Y axes (not necessarily time). chart count over host by status: host on X-axis, status as separate series. timechart: X-axis is always _time (time buckets). chart: general purpose. timechart: time-series analysis
questions.explanation: chart count OVER X_FIELD BY split_field: X-field can be any field (not just time). Useful for: non-time charts (CPU by host, errors by user). timechart: X always time. chart example: | chart avg(cpu) over host by day_of_week: CPU per host per weekday. split limit: top N series. useother=false: don't group others.

questions.question: What is Splunk IT Service Intelligence (ITSI)?
options: A premium app built on Splunk that provides service-level monitoring — models business services as hierarchical trees of KPIs. Service health scores. Machine learning for anomaly detection. Episode Review: correlates events into incidents. AIOps features
questions.explanation: ITSI: builds on Splunk platform. Services: define business services with KPIs (from SPL searches). Health score: 0-100 per service. Tree: Business Service depends on → Application Services → Infrastructure KPIs. Anomaly detection: ML baselines. Episodes: correlated alerts needing investigation. Glass tables: custom NOC visualizations.

questions.question: What is a Splunk Forwarder and what types exist?
options: Agent installed on data sources to collect and send logs to Splunk indexers — Universal Forwarder (UF): lightweight, minimal Splunk, just forwards raw data. Heavy Forwarder (HF): full Splunk, can parse/filter/route data before forwarding
questions.explanation: Universal Forwarder (UF): 8-10 MB, monitors files/logs, sends to indexers. No local processing. Deploy everywhere. Heavy Forwarder (HF): full Splunk, parse/transform/route before forwarding. Use HF for: data masking, protocol aggregation, network syslog collection. Deployment Server: manages UF configurations at scale.

questions.question: What is the Splunk Deployment Server?
options: Manages and pushes configurations (apps, inputs.conf, outputs.conf) to Universal Forwarders at scale — deployment client: forwarder that polls deployment server for updates. App: configuration package. Server class: group of forwarders receiving same app
questions.explanation: Deployment Server: not a Splunk server tier (can be any Splunk instance). Manages: forwarder configs. App: folder with configs. Server class: maps apps to forwarder groups. Forwarder: phoneHome interval (check for updates). Supports: 10,000+ forwarders per deployment server. Alternative for cloud: Splunk Cloud uses Splunk Web inputs or HEC.

questions.question: What is Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC)?
options: REST API endpoint for sending events directly to Splunk via HTTP/HTTPS — no forwarder needed. Applications, containers, IoT devices send JSON payloads directly. Token-based authentication. Use for: application logging, cloud services, webhooks
questions.explanation: HEC: endpoint at :8088/services/collector. POST JSON: {event: {key: value}, source: 'myapp', sourcetype: 'json'}. Token: generated in Splunk web, passed in Authorization header. Raw endpoint: /collector/raw for plain text. Use for: Docker log driver, Lambda functions, GitHub webhooks, any HTTP-capable source. High-throughput capable.

questions.question: What is the Splunk append command?
options: Appends results from a subsearch to the current results — creates a combined result set. Unlike join (field matching), append just adds rows. Use for: compare two time periods, add totals row, combine different data sources into one table
questions.explanation: append: | append [search index=web earliest=-7d@d | stats count as last_week_count]. Adds last week's count rows to current results. Results: combined rows from both. appendcols: adds columns (fields) from subsearch. appendpipe: apply pipe to results, append back. Use for: adding comparison data, adding header/footer rows.

questions.question: What is Splunk's Knowledge Object sharing level?
options: App: available only in the current app context. Global: available in all apps. Private: only the creating user. Sharing affects: saved searches, dashboards, lookups, macros, field extractions. Admin can change sharing. Default: private for users, app for admins
questions.explanation: Knowledge object sharing: Private (only your user), App (all users in this app), Global (all apps). Change via: Settings > Knowledge Objects > select type > Edit permissions. Apps: Splunk organizes knowledge objects. Default Search App: home. ES: objects in SplunkEnterpriseSecuritySuite app. Best practice: share at app level, promote to global when needed cross-app.

questions.question: What is the Splunk props.conf file used for?
options: Configures how Splunk parses and processes data at index time — event line breaking, timestamp recognition, source type configuration, field transformations (REPORT-, EXTRACT-, FIELDALIAS-). Critical for correct data parsing
questions.explanation: props.conf: stanza [sourcetype_name] or [source::path/to/file]. Settings: TIME_PREFIX (find timestamp), TIME_FORMAT (strptime format), LINE_BREAKER (event boundary regex), SHOULD_LINEMERGE (multiline events), EXTRACT-fieldname (regex). Works with transforms.conf: REPORT-name = transform_name → lookup in transforms.conf.

questions.question: What are Splunk search best practices for performance?
options: Use earliest/latest time range, specify index and sourcetype early in search, use tstats for large volumes, avoid ORs on high-cardinality fields, filter events before transforming (search before stats), use NOT vs !=, avoid wildcards at start of search terms
questions.explanation: Performance tips: (1) Specify time range (limits data scanned). (2) index=X sourcetype=Y early (bloom filter). (3) Add specific field filters before |. (4) Use tstats for data model data. (5) Avoid leading wildcards (src=*domain.com slow). (6) stats before head/tail. (7) Use lookup instead of subsearch join. (8) Avoid transaction (prefer stats).

questions.question: What is Splunk's field alias and why use it?
options: A knowledge object that creates an alternate name for an existing field — allows referencing the same data with different field names for CIM normalization. Different from rename (which is search-time only)
questions.explanation: Field alias (FIELDALIAS in props.conf): normalize vendor-specific field names to CIM. FIELDALIAS-cim_src = source_address AS src. Now 'src' works instead of 'source_address'. Persistent, not search-time. Different from: rename (temp rename in search), eval field=other_field (creates new, keeps old). Used for: CIM normalization, backward compatibility.

questions.question: What is Splunk's Risk-Based Alerting (RBA)?
options: Security framework that assigns risk scores to entities (users, hosts) based on suspicious behavior — many low-priority alerts → risk score accumulates → alert when entity crosses risk threshold. Reduces alert fatigue vs per-event alerting
questions.explanation: RBA (Splunk ES): correlation searches assign risk_score to risk_object (user/system). Risk events stored in risk index. Aggregate: when user's total risk > threshold → Risk Notable Event. Advantages: catches low-and-slow attacks that don't trigger individual rules. Reduces noise: many low-fidelity signals → one high-confidence alert.

questions.question: What is Splunk Observability Cloud?
options: Splunk's APM/infrastructure monitoring platform — OpenTelemetry-native, metrics/traces/logs in one platform. Features: APM (distributed tracing), Infrastructure Monitoring (metrics from hosts, containers), Log Observer (log analytics). Separate from Splunk Enterprise
questions.explanation: Splunk Observability Cloud (formerly SignalFx): cloud-native monitoring. APM: distributed traces, service maps, latency analysis. Infrastructure: host metrics, K8s monitoring, cloud service metrics. Synthetics: URL/API synthetic testing. Log Observer: stream log analysis. OpenTelemetry: primary collection method. Separate product from Splunk Enterprise/Cloud.

questions.question: What is the Splunk subsearch and its limitations?
options: A search nested within brackets inside a main search — results of subsearch used in main search (usually generating a search filter). Example: [search index=blocklist | return 100 ip] searches for events where IP matches blocklist result. Limits: 10,000 results, 60 second timeout
questions.explanation: Subsearch: [search conditions | fields value_field | format] — generates search filter dynamically. Limit: 10,000 results, 60s max. Performance: subsearch runs first, then main. Better alternatives for static data: lookup. For dynamic data: join. Format command: converts subsearch results to proper boolean filter. Used in: threat hunting, dynamic allow/blocklists.

questions.question: What is Splunk's dispatch directory and search artifacts?
options: Directory where Splunk stores search results temporarily ($SPLUNK_HOME/var/run/splunk/dispatch) — each search creates a job with unique ID, stores results in dispatch. Search artifacts expire based on TTL. High dispatch counts: performance impact
questions.explanation: Dispatch: search job results stored here. Auto-cleanup after TTL (default 7-10 days). Large dispatch: disk space and I/O impact. Artifacts: .csv result files, search.log, lookup results. Jobs Dashboard: Splunk Web > Activity > Jobs. Saved search acceleration: cached results in dispatch. Monitor disk space on search heads.

questions.question: What is the Splunk return command?
options: Used in subsearches to format results as a filter for the outer search — return 100 field: returns up to 100 values as (field=val1 OR field=val2...). Default: returns all found values. Part of subsearch pipeline
questions.explanation: return: in subsearch, formats output. | return 100 src_ip → (src_ip=1.2.3.4 OR src_ip=5.6.7.8...). Outer search uses this as filter. Without return: subsearch uses format command (default). Use return explicitly to control field name and count. Alternative: | fields fieldname (return without format command).

questions.question: What is Splunk's index=_internal and why is it useful?
options: Internal Splunk telemetry index — stores Splunk operational data: indexing performance, search performance, license usage, forwarder connection stats, errors. Used for: monitoring Splunk health, troubleshooting data ingestion issues, license management
questions.explanation: _internal: Splunk's own operational data. Key searches: index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd_stderr: Splunk errors. index=_internal sourcetype=metrics group=thruput: indexing throughput. index=_internal sourcetype=license_usage: license consumption per host. index=_internal sourcetype=splunk_web_access: web UI access. Essential for Splunk administrators.

questions.question: What is Splunk's Search Factor vs Replication Factor?
options: Replication Factor (RF): how many copies of raw data buckets exist across indexer cluster peers — data availability. Search Factor (SF): how many copies are in searchable format — SF ≤ RF. If peer fails: still have SF searchable copies elsewhere. RF=3, SF=2 is typical
questions.explanation: RF: total data copies. SF: searchable copies (with tsidx index files). Peer fails: RF ensures data not lost, SF ensures search continues without rebuilding. Typical: RF=3, SF=2. Bucket states: hot (active indexing), warm (searchable), cold (searchable, slower), frozen (archived/deleted). Smart Store: tiered storage for warm/cold on object storage.

questions.question: What is Splunk's role-based access control and key roles?
options: Roles define capabilities and index/app access: admin (full access), power (save reports, create alerts, use lookups), user (search, basic features). Add-on roles: can_delete, schedule_search, edit_lookups. Custom roles: inherit from existing, add restrictions
questions.explanation: Key roles: admin (all capabilities, all indexes), power (create/save searches, edit lookups, accelerate data models), user (basic search, save private objects). Capabilities: specific permissions (can_delete, edit_roles, schedule_search). Index access: add indexes to role. Inheritance: user role inherits from... Role stacking: user has multiple roles.

questions.question: What is Splunk's Adaptive Response Framework?
options: Enables correlation searches (Splunk ES) to trigger automated response actions — when notable event created, automatically execute: run script, send to ticketing system, quarantine endpoint (via Splunk SOAR), email analyst. Framework for security automation
questions.explanation: Adaptive Response (AR): ES correlation search → AR actions. Actions: create JIRA ticket, send to Splunk SOAR for playbook execution, email, run custom script, update threat intelligence. Enables: security orchestration from within Splunk ES. Partners: Carbon Black quarantine, AWS Lambda execution, ServiceNow incident creation.

questions.question: What is the Splunk map command?
options: Applies a search to each result from the previous search — map maxsearches=10 search='search index=web host=$host$ | stats count by status'. For each host in results, run sub-search. Different from join/append — runs separate search per result
questions.explanation: map: runs one search per row from previous results, substituting field values ($fieldname$). Powerful but expensive — avoid on large result sets. maxsearches: limit parallel searches. Use for: drill-down enrichment, per-host detailed analysis. Alternative: subsearch (one search returns filter for all), join (one search, field match). map: true per-row search execution.

questions.question: What is Splunk's KV Store?
options: A NoSQL store built into Splunk for storing and retrieving operational data — collections of key-value JSON documents. Used by: apps, lookups (dynamic), Splunk ES (threat intelligence, investigation status). Access: REST API, SPL inputlookup/outputlookup, JavaScript
questions.explanation: KV Store: per-collection NoSQL JSON store. App data: store state, configuration, user preferences. Dynamic lookup: backed by KV Store, can be updated via API. REST API: GET/POST/DELETE /servicesNS/app/collection/record. SPL: | inputlookup kv_collection | outputlookup kv_collection. JS: KV Store App Framework API. Replicated across SHC members.

questions.question: What is Splunk's threat intelligence framework?
options: Splunk ES feature that ingests threat indicators (IP, URL, domain, file hash) from feeds — STIX/TAXII, CSV, API. Matches against network/endpoint data automatically. Generates threat activity alerts. Sources: MISP, commercial feeds, ISAC
questions.explanation: Threat Intel: ES → Threat Intelligence Management. Sources: TAXII (STIX), structured CSV, custom REST. Lookup-based matching: intel against network/auth events. Alerts: when known malicious IP seen, known bad hash executed. Update schedule: hourly/daily. Custom indicators: manually add IOCs. Intel sources: AV engines, government ISAC, dark web monitors.
